name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateReactionC
summary: Per-frame reaction step: switches on the state word at +0x38 - states 8 and 0x10 play SE 0xE4E through the sound player, state 0x1A removes key 4 from the small keyed list at +0x2C - and always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of the unnamed callee 0x006D334C shows a small keyed-list remove (bounds r1 < 5, count at +0x1C, entries at +0x14), so the second branch is 'drop list key 4', not a transform. It still has no caller and no vtable slot, so the gimmick/reaction attribution stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_Cue_ResetIfIdle
summary: When the sound player's state byte at +4 has bit 3 clear, resets the cue to its neutral state: clears +0x14 and copies the two default words at 0x0072A79C+0x68/+0x6C into cue+4 and cue+8.
evidence: NEW: Sound_GetPlayer is the lazy sound-player singleton (353 callers, PlaySE/PrepareBGM/SetVolumeSE), so the bit test is a sound-system state/idle flag rather than a UI flag; the object's identity as a cue still rests on the neighbouring maybe_ names.

name: maybe_Sound_SetGainFromValue
summary: Sound gain wrapper: fetches the sound player singleton, reinterprets the u32 argument as a float (VectorUnsignedToFloat) and forwards it with the first argument to the gain setter 0x001ED7CC.
evidence: NEW: the body only uses Sound_GetPlayer and a target in the Snd_ range next to the named Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle (0x001EDF88); nothing in it is UI. The target 0x001ED7CC is not a Ghidra entry point, so which gain (voice/BGM) it sets remains unproven - hence corrected and kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_IsSoundHandleActive
summary: Returns the flow node itself when the sound player's table at +0x1848 still has an entry whose first word equals node->f_1B4->f_78, otherwise 0; a per-node keep-alive test.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x0063071C shows a search of 8-byte entries at soundPlayer+0x1848 for the key in r1, so the test is against the sound system, not a selected row/actor - the old 'IsRowActorSelected' named the wrong system. The only support for the flow-node role is the table entry 0x00726F90.

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_ApplyVolumeFromField
summary: Fetches the sound player and applies the value stored at self+0x1A8 (converted to float) through the sound volume setter 0x001EE018; returns self.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x001EE018 scales the incoming s0 float, converts it to int and stores the sound player's volume/state byte, so this branch sets a volume, it does not play an SE - the old 'PlaySeForState' was wrong. The object is only known as a flow-table entry (0x00727078).

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_IsEntryUsable
summary: Gates a flow entry value: reads the sound player's current id (field +0x58, or +0x64 when state bit 1 is set), treats out-of-range values (>= 0x9E or 0xFF) as unusable, and returns 0 when the player is in the state reported by 0x006305F0; otherwise returns value unchanged.
evidence: NEW: 0x006305F0 is a pure predicate on the sound player's byte +0x10A50 (true for state 2 or 3), not an entry-acceptance helper; the range checks on +0x58/+0x64 are as described before. No caller, so both the entry role and the return convention remain inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeInfo_TickCraft
summary: Sound-gated step: while the sound player still has the id stored at self+0x224 and the widget at self+0x2F0 is idle (+0x28 == 0), requests step 7 on the script object at self+0x11C and commits it; always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: 0x0062F680 (asm) is 'returns 1 when obj+0x28 == 0', an idle test, and 0x0063071C is the sound-player table lookup - so this is a sound/animation-gated script step. The RecipeInfo/craft attribution still rests only on the first pass, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeInfo_TickCraftB
summary: Second copy of the sound-gated step: same sound id at self+0x224, same idle widget at self+0x2F0 and same step-7 request on the script object at self+0x11C, returning 1.
evidence: NEW: byte-identical to 0x00450550 except for the function address (a template copy); the callee names (Ui_AnimRefList-style widget idle test + sound lookup) confirm the step shape, but nothing names the alternate recipe slot.

name: maybe_Sound_ApplyPendingVolume
summary: Three-instruction sound thunk: fetches the sound player singleton and hands the float argument (arriving in s0 and dropped by Ghidra) to the volume setter 0x001EE018.
evidence: NEW: the body is exactly 0x002DD7E0 minus the field load, and 0x001EE018 (asm 0x001EE018) scales the s0 float and stores the player's volume/state - so 'TalkWindow_PushEvent' was wrong. The float parameter is invisible in the readable C, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TalkWindow_CanHandleEvent
summary: Unless the sound player's byte +4 bit 3 is set, asks the script/command object at self+0x11C to accept event 0x0C (virtual +0x14) and commits it (virtual +0x10); always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: unlike 0x00465DD4 this body really does push an event - the same virtual +0x14/+0x10 pair on self+0x11C that maybe_Ui_Window_SyncRecordAndAdvance uses - while Sound_GetPlayer is only the gate. The window class is still unproven, so maybe_ stands.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_NutTask_Ctor
signature: u32* maybe_Actor_Action_NutTask_Ctor(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, const char* tag)
summary: Constructor of an action-family task: shared Action_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x00759638, stores effect id 0x1E at +0x2C and the negated global direction vector 0x007E7030 at +0x30..+0x38, clearing +0x3C and +0x10.
evidence: NEW: Actor_CreateBehaviourTasks (0x0022FBD8) creates the 0x44-byte task in slot 1 through this factory and passes the ASCII tag 0x74756E = 'nut' (the same table passes 'run', 'jump', 'follow', 'f2n'), so N_044's 'Emote' label is not supported. The tag may name the animation rather than the task, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Action_StateSequence4_Ctor
summary: Action-subclass constructor: runs Action_CtorBase, installs g_actionSubclass4AnimVtable, then builds the embedded state-sequence object at +0x2C (vtable g_stateSequence62Vtable, back-pointer to the action) and default-constructs its four 0x18-byte states with ctor 0x006C7978.
evidence: NEW: the 4 x 0x18 construction and the state-sequence vtable are literal, and std_StateSequence62_Tick still names this ctor as its owner; no caller string or vtable names the concrete action, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_Action_CreateDig
summary: Minimal action-subclass constructor: runs Action_CtorBase and installs vtable 0x007595D0; the paired start routine is 0x001BA3F4 and the vtable sits in the 0x00759xxx action block with the Nut and task tables.
evidence: NEW: still only a bare vtable store. The call-graph caller 0x0022E494 is a 4 KB Thumb chunk whose callee list already mixes unrelated actor/action functions, so it does not identify this factory; the 'Dig' label remains the first pass's vtable-block reading.

name: maybe_Field_Action_CreateNut
summary: Minimal action-subclass constructor: runs Action_CtorBase and installs vtable 0x00759604 (the table right after the Dig action's); handlers live at 0x001BA510 and 0x001BA5D0.
evidence: NEW: unchanged - nothing in this body distinguishes it from the Dig factory except the vtable constant, and the attributed caller 0x0022E494 is an unreliable mixed Thumb chunk. The Nut label still comes from the first-pass vtable block.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateEffectSlots
summary: Updates the 72 (0x48) per-slot effects via 0x003CA6DC, then - if any of the 8 formation entries at BattleScene+0x30+idx*0x2C has type 0x21 - rolls 1..100 per entry in self->f_DE00 with the battle RNG and spawns the slot effect (0x003C91DC) when the roll is <= the entry's threshold at +0xBB08.
evidence: NEW: the byte range was re-checked against the assembly (loop 0..0x47, then 8 x 0x2C formation entries, then f_DE00 units at 0x68 stride) and the named callees Battle_Ui_SpawnSlotEffectB/Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessState5 confirm an effect-slot update plus a random trigger. The name only covers the first half but is not wrong, so kept at maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyStatus_CacheCostume
summary: One-shot cache for the battle party panel: on the first call it resolves the member record for panel->f_768 (party-member getter 0x0035EB98) and copies the member's equipped-costume byte (+0xE5) to panel+0xB18A, then sets the cached flag at +0xB189.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x0035EB98 is the party-member record accessor and member+0xE5 is the equipped costume id (FACTS.md), so the cached byte is the costume, not an unnamed 'status value'. The panel class is still inferred from the layout.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoChildObject_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a vtable-0x00768484 object owning two 0x16C-byte UI children: allocates each from the UI heap, builds it with the base ctor plus vtable 0x0076AC20 / 0x0076ABD0 and its anim-ref list at +0x11C, registers both through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable and stores them at self[1]/self[2].
evidence: NEW: the body builds two complete children (Mem_AllocAligned_2 + base ctor + CreatePartsFromTable, freeing on failure), so it is not a 'panel ctor' of a standalone panel; the two-child shape and both child vtables are literal, but the class behind vtable 0x00768484 is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_RowObject_CtorB
summary: Small row-object constructor: Ui_Object_CtorBase, vtable 0x007662B0, constructs the animation-ref list at +0x4C and sets the visible flag at +0x50.
evidence: NEW: its caller is the confident Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor (0.60), which builds it as one of the tactics-screen parts, so the 'row object of the sakusen window' reading holds; the concrete row class name is still unknown and 'B' remains an ordinal.

name: maybe_Ui_TabBar_Ctor
summary: UI object constructor: Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs the class vtable, then chains three Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor calls at +0x4C/+0x9C/+0xEC and returns the object base.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the now-named Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor and it is called exactly three times, matching the previous 'three lists = tab bar' reading; there is still no caller and the vtable is an unresolved global, so the class stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimObject_Ctor
summary: Shared animation-object initialiser: stores the caller-supplied vtable, builds two animation-ref lists (+0x14 and +0x64), points the three frame cursors (+0x50/+0x54/+0x58) at the default frame and clears the state words.
evidence: NEW: the only callee is the named Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor (called twice) and the vtable arrives as an argument, so this is a base-class/member initialiser; no caller can name the concrete class.

name: maybe_Menu_InitLayoutNode
summary: Shared node initialiser: writes the vtable/id passed in into word 0, constructs the animation-ref list at +0x14, sets its +0x50 flag and clears the four words before it.
evidence: NEW: same shape as 0x001D8478 but with the vtable stored into word 0; it is vtable slot 1 of a 10-entry table with no direct caller, so the menu/layout-node attribution remains a guess.

name: Ui_EquipPart_Ctor
summary: Constructor of one part of the equip window: installs the part vtable, runs the C++ static-init guard, copies the three default size triples into the part (+0x34..+0x3C and +0x64/+0x68), constructs the anim-ref list at +0x6C and fills three 0xC-byte sub-blocks with the default triples.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the equip-window sub-part factory (0x003331A8, maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_InitSubParts), which chains this ctor four times, and the body writes the part vtable at +0; that supports the equip-part role even though which visual part (frame/icon) it is stays unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoListObject_Ctor
summary: Member initialiser that constructs two animation-reference lists 0x50 bytes apart inside the caller's object (the first pointer is forwarded untouched, the second is built at +0x50) and returns the object base.
evidence: NEW: the callee is Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor (0.6) and the first argument is forwarded but dropped by Ghidra (in_r0), showing this is a member initialiser, not an allocator; no caller and no vtable, so the class is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_PartSlot_InitEmbedded
summary: Constructs an embedded object with two animation-ref lists: stores the vtable/owner words, builds the first list at +8 and the second at +0x60, links both intrusive list heads to themselves and copies the default timing/owner pair; returns the base 0x58 bytes before the argument.
evidence: NEW: Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor is named and called twice, and the relative-offset construction is literal; no caller or vtable names the owning class, so the PartSlot label is still the first pass's guess.

name: maybe_Ui_EmotionBalloon_Init
summary: Initialises an owner-plus-list object: stores the owner pointer at +0, clears +4 and constructs the animation-ref list at +8, returning the object base.
evidence: NEW: the only callee is the named Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor; the balloon attribution still comes from the paired balloon code (no caller, vtable or string here names the class), so maybe_ stands.

name: maybe_Sound_ApplyCategoryBgmState
signature: void maybe_Sound_ApplyCategoryBgmState(u32 unused, u32 category, int soundId)
summary: Routes a sound by category: looks the id up in the sound table (func_0063F1E0), finds the 2-byte {category, mode} row and applies the mode - 1 stops the pending BGM (Snd_StopPendingBgm + 0x001EE220), 2 does nothing, anything else applies the pending volume through 0x001EE018; categories 3/4 default to mode 2 when no row matches.
evidence: NEW: the named callees are Snd_StopPendingBgm, Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle and the volume setter 0x001EE018, and the record is a category->mode table, so the function routes a sound's category; it does not select a BGM track as 'SetBgmForCategory' claimed. All eight callers are still mid-confidence menu param helpers, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_PartySlots_NotifyChanged
summary: Slot-change notification for the battle party/target-marker table: forwards to maybe_Menu_OnSlotChanged and, when the battle work is in 3D mode (+0x4244), refreshes the actor's slot with 0x0020B990 and builds a 4 x 8-byte record array filled with 0xFF.
evidence: NEW: 0x0020B990 (asm) tests the same five 0x40-stride slot ids at +0x4C/+0x8C/+0xCC/+0x10C/+0x14C, and std_ConstructArray is a genuine 4-element construction (FACTS: the CRT helper is mis-marked noreturn), so the old 'assert/unexpected path' reading was wrong. Callers Battle_TargetMarker_Update and Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshMembers fix the battle context, but the object class is still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshMemberSlots
summary: Walks the battle unit list at battleWork+0x4260 and, for each living unit, reads the three u8 ids at unit+0xB115/+0xB135/+0xB155 (0x20 stride), resolves each one through the record table and stores the id with Menu_Slot_StoreActorId only when the resolved record's +0x2F2 byte is set.
evidence: NEW: the caller Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshMembers and the storage callee Menu_Slot_StoreActorId support the party-slot refresh reading; the three ids and the record table are still unidentified, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Menu_ClaimFreeSlotForId
signature: void maybe_Menu_ClaimFreeSlotForId(void* self, u32 id, u32 unused, u32 stack)
summary: If the id is not already in the five 0x40-byte slot records (+0x4C..+0x14C), claims the first free record (bytes +0x0C/+0x0D == -1 and u16 id +0x0E == 0xFFFF), stamps the id into it, clears +0x08, sets +0x10 = -1 and finally refreshes the entry's icon through maybe_Menu_UpdateItemIcon.
evidence: NEW: caller maybe_BattlePartyWindow_ClaimPartySlots and the five-slot membership scan make the claim role solid; whether the slots hold party members or item entries is still open (the icon refresh suggests a UI entry), so maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_BuildMemberMask
signature: unsigned maybe_Battle_BuildMemberMask(void* self, unsigned actorIndex, int includeInactive)
summary: Builds the party-member bitmask for a battle action: walks the four unit slots at battleWork+0x4254, accumulates 1 << actorBit (0x00639B74) for live, non-hidden units and remembers actorIndex's bit, then builds the usable-slot mask and verifies that none of the 0x59 slots is set.
evidence: NEW: both callers are battle UIs (Ui_BattleCommandWindow_InitDisplay, Battle_Ui_RefreshPartyNameLines) and the body walks battle work +0x5C/+0x4254, so the old 'Menu_' prefix was wrong. The mask's consumer is still unnamed, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_InitSubWindows
summary: Initialises the battle command window's three sub-windows through builder 0x003D20DC (indices 0/2/3), clears the selection byte and then selects entry 1 through the object's virtual +0x18.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Ui_BattleCommandWindow_InitDisplay, but both builders stay unnamed, so which three sub-windows these are is still inferred; kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_InitSubWindowsB
summary: Variant of 0x003D2084 that initialises the same three sub-windows through builder 0x003D2300 (indices 0/2/3), clears the selection byte and selects entry 1 through virtual +0x18.
evidence: NEW: same shape, same named caller (Ui_BattleCommandWindow_InitDisplay) and only the builder differs (0x003D2300 vs 0x003D20DC); with both builders unnamed, the two variants cannot be told apart (2D/3D?), so maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor2D_ResetIfRegistered
summary: If the two-key field-actor table lookup 0x00629A24(work+0x24A98, *(u16*)(work+0x27C5C), actor+0x298) finds the actor, calls actor virtuals +0x40 and +0x58 with the argument 4 and clears actor+0x288 and actor+0x2D8.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x00629A24 shows a bounded two-key table search (8-byte stride entries, u16 key at +0xC0 and a second id), not an item-bag query; the named callers (talk-party command handlers, Actor2D create variants, event-state change) all fit a 'reset/leave if registered' step. The names 'ResetSpansIfIdle' described neither the key search nor the virtual calls, hence corrected.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor body of a very large composite window: resets its vtable and then destroys the roughly forty embedded sub-objects in reverse order (layout refs, message pages, panel/icon arrays, render nodes); there is no operator delete at the end.
evidence: NEW: every callee is a destructor (Ui_Object_DtorBase, Ui_MessagePage_Dtor, Ui_LayoutRef_Release, Pack_ReleaseHandle, std_destroy_range) and the body keeps subtracting the member offsets, so this is one big destructor, not the 'ConstructParts' chain the first pass read.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorB
summary: Non-deleting destructor of a large composite window: resets the vtable, then destroys the embedded message pages, layout refs and child arrays (0x5C x 4, 0x50 x 5) in reverse order.
evidence: NEW: same destructor pattern as 0x002609E0 (std_destroy_range + Ui_Object_DtorBase chain, no free) and its only caller is the deleting destructor 0x00264CE0, which confirms this is the dtor body, not a constructor. The concrete window class is still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorC
summary: Non-deleting destructor of a large composite window (vtable-0x001F0700 family): destroys the embedded sub-widget at +0xA5A, the message pages, layout refs, the 8 x 0x3C array and the 0x50-stride child arrays, ending in the deleting base helper.
evidence: NEW: all eight callees are destructor helpers (Ui_Object_DtorBase, Ui_MessagePage_Dtor, Ui_LayoutRef_Release, std_destroy_range, Ui_Object_DtorThenFree_NoVtable, ...) and the function is a vtable slot, so the first-pass 'InitPartsK' had the direction wrong. Class unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorD
summary: Destructor fragment of a large window: resets the vtable and the embedded 0x7B0-byte region, releases two layout references, destroys two 0x414-byte panel arrays (count 2 each) and the embedded message page, then runs the layout-element teardown.
evidence: NEW: the callee set is exactly the destructor chain (Ui_Object_DtorBase, Ui_LayoutRef_Release, std_destroy_range, Ui_MessagePage_Dtor) and it ends in func_001D8C2C rather than a constructor call, so 'InitPartsC' was the wrong direction. No string or vtable names the window class.

name: Ui_Window_DtorWithPanelArrays
summary: Deleting destructor of a window that owns two arrays of 0x414-byte Ui_Panel objects plus an embedded message page: releases the layout refs, destroys both arrays and the embedded objects, runs the base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: the body ends in func_0010F6CC (operator delete) after Ui_Object_DtorBase, sits in the window base-class block after Ui_Window_CtorBase/CtorBaseEx, and the two 0x414 panels are literal (std_destroy_range size 0x414 count 2). The concrete class is irrelevant to this helper role.

name: Ui_Window_DtorWithTwoPanels
summary: Shared deleting destructor for windows owning a two-element Ui_Panel array: destroys the 2 x 0x414 array at self+0x78, runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees the window.
evidence: NEW: disassembly 0x002A45D8 shows a deleting destructor: store the class vtable into [self], std_destroy_range(self+0x78, dtor 0x001F0700, size 0x414, count 2), Ui_Object_DtorBase(self) and a tail call to the free routine 0x0010F6CC. The mechanics are literal, so the helper name is exact; vtable 0x0077FCCC is a shared base table, so no concrete class is claimed.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateState
summary: Per-frame update of the status window: bails while the window is busy, waits for the transition state at self[2], handles the 0x4A8/0x4AA/0x94 flags, and in state 3 rebuilds the party summary bytes written to GameWork+0x2E2F4/+0x2E2F5 (active-slot count and a second-row value) before setting state 0x3D.
evidence: NEW: named callees Ui_Window_SetState, Ui_StatusWindow_CountActiveSlots and Party_GetSecondRowNameLength support the status-window reading; the only caller is maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_CreatePartB, so the owning window is still not pinned.

name: Ui_TwelveRowTextWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a twelve-row text/list window: chains the Ui_Object_CtorSmall base, installs vtable 0x0075EB0C, builds the scroller sub-object at +0x54 (type 0x0C) and default-constructs twelve 0x10-byte row records.
evidence: NEW: the paired destructor 0x0029DDAC stores the same vtable 0x0075EB0C and destroys exactly 12 x 0x10 rows, and the family sibling Ui_TenRowTextWindow_Ctor uses the same base/scroller with ten 0xC rows - the row count is literal.

name: maybe_Ui_Composite_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a composite list object: resets the two intrusive child-list heads and their sentinels, destroys the 0x78 x 0x0E and 0x50 x 3 child arrays, then runs the list-window base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: the body is a destructor by its callees (std_destroy_range, maybe_Ui_ListWindow_DtorBase) and ends in the free helper; the owning class (vtable-0x0075EB0C family) is still unknown, so maybe_.

name: Ui_TwelveRowTextWindow_DtorDeleting
summary: Deleting destructor of the twelve-row text window: reinstalls vtable 0x0075EB0C, destroys the twelve 0x10-byte row records at +0x1C, runs the list-window base destructor and frees the instance.
evidence: NEW: it pairs with the constructor 0x0029DD44 (same vtable, same 12 x 0x10 array) and with the named Ui_TenRowTextWindow family, and the row count 0xC is visible in std_destroy_range(..., 0x10, 0xC).

name: Ui_Window_BuildMessageArgFromToken
signature: void Ui_Window_BuildMessageArgFromToken(void* self, u32 token, u32 tokenType)
summary: Converts a control-token chain into button-icon message arguments: the token type byte selects icon resource 0x4D..0x51 (0x50 becomes 0x51 when only one party member is alive), stores it at self+4, applies it with Ui_SakusenWindow_BuildMessageArgs, and keeps pulling the next token while the chain continues.
evidence: NEW: the caller Ui_Window_GetMessageArg and the callee Ui_SakusenWindow_BuildMessageArgs are now confidently named, and the token->icon mapping is literal (0x4D..0x51 plus the Party_CountAliveMembers special case).

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_BuildMessageArgsTail
summary: Not a real entry point: 0x002A2C0C is the second bl plus the epilogue inside Ui_SakusenWindow_BuildMessageArgs (0x002A29A8); the symbol only exists so the merge does not create a bogus function.
evidence: NEW: unchanged - the body is still halt_baddata(), its sole caller is the parent function, and the assembly shows a mid-function sequence (bl 0x1902A4; add sp; pop {...pc}), not a callable start.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_HandlePaneEvent
signature: void maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_HandlePaneEvent(void* self, u32 p1, u32 p2, u32 p3)
summary: Pane event handler for the tactics window's two panes at +0x160/+0x17C: swaps visibility when the active pane is hidden, otherwise dispatches on the pane event mask - bit 4 disables the 3D view and advances the command queue, bit 1 executes the pane's text command (0..3), bit 0x10 consumes a ring-buffer entry - and records the result in the pane/command state.
evidence: NEW: named callees Ui_SakusenWindow_Set3DViewEnabled, Text_ExecuteCommand, Container_RingBuffer_Next and Ui_CommandQueue_AdvanceAlt support the handler reading; there is no direct caller, so the class attribution is still inferred and the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ClearPendingInputA
summary: If Container_RingBuffer_Next reports another queued input event, clears the pending-input word at UiCore+0x94.
evidence: NEW: both callees are named (Container_RingBuffer_Next, Ui_GetCore) and the twin 0x00387058 has the same body; the argument passed in r3 is still dropped and nothing names the window, so the descriptive A/B names stay at maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ClearPendingInputB
summary: Copy of 0x00382AD0: when Container_RingBuffer_Next reports another queued input event it clears the pending-input word at UiCore+0x94.
evidence: NEW: identical 52-byte body to 0x00382AD0 with the same two named callees; the two copies are used by different windows, so a single class cannot be named.

name: Field_ActorAction_Exit_Ctor
signature: void Field_ActorAction_Exit_Ctor(void* self, void* owner, void* model, const char* name, u32 flag)
summary: Constructor of the field actor's 'exit' action: runs the shared Field_ActorMotion_Ctor base, installs the action vtable, then builds the embedded four-state sequence at +0x2C (state vtable, back-pointer) and default-constructs its four 0x18-byte states.
evidence: NEW: Field_ActorActionSet_Init (0x00399834) calls this ctor for the 0xD8-byte action slot and passes the ASCII tag 0x74697865 = 'exit' (the same table passes 'nut', 'run', 'jump', 'skill'), so the previous 'ActionSet4' name described the wrong object - it is the exit action, not a set.

name: Ui_EnsureSubObject
summary: Lazy child creation: when self+0x48 is null, allocates a 0x1D4-byte object from the UI heap, constructs it with Ui_GuideWindow_Ctor, registers it through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable (freeing it again on failure) and stores it at self+0x48 with +0x94 cleared.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the declared Ui_GuideWindow_Ctor and the 0x1D4 allocation matches it; caller 0x00626BC8's init branch plus the null check confirm a one-time ensure rather than a per-frame build. The generic name is kept because the owner class is not named.
